name: Melchizedek
overview: Melchizedek is a male figure known as the King of Salem and a priest of God Most High, as described in Genesis 14:18. His unique role combines both royal and priestly offices, highlighting a distinctive position in the biblical narrative. No tribe or additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Melchizedek means 'my king is right' or 'righteous,' indicating a title of kingly authority. He is also called the 'King of Salem,' meaning 'king of completeness or peace,' and identified as a 'priest of God Most High,' emphasizing his priestly service to the supreme God. These titles together reveal his dual role as both ruler and spiritual leader.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Melchizedek beyond what is listed in his unique attribute as King of Salem and priest of God Most High. No further relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Melchizedek's significance lies in his unique combination of kingship and priesthood, serving as a priest to the Most High God while reigning as king. This dual role sets a precedent in the biblical text, highlighting a figure who bridges political and spiritual authority. His appearance in Genesis 14:18 introduces a model of priesthood that is distinct from later Levitical lines, underscoring his importance in the biblical narrative.
